sanskrit: dāsapatnīr ahigopā atiṣṭhan niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ | apāṃ bilam apihitaṃ yad āsīd vṛtraṃ jaghanvām̐ apa tad vavāra ||
english: The waters, guarded by the serpent, stood blocked, mastered by the Paṇi-lord like cattle penned. The aperture of the waters that had been stopped up — he who smote Vṛtra swept that aside.

sanskrit: aśvyo vāro abhavas tad indra sṛke yat tvā pratyahan deva ekaḥ | ajayo gā ajayaḥ śūra somam avāsṛjaḥ sartave sapta sindhūn ||
english: That became a horse-hair noose for thee, O Indra, wherein the one god struck back at thee with a tusk. Thou didst win the cattle, thou didst win the Soma, O hero; thou didst loose the seven rivers to flow.

sanskrit: nāsmai vidyun na tanyatuḥ śiṣedha na yāmyaham akirad dhrāduniṃ ca indraś ca yad yuyudhāte ahiś ca- -utāparībhyo maghavā vi jigye ||
english: Neither lightning nor thunder could restrain him; Yamī dispersed neither mist nor hailstorm against him. When Indra and the serpent fought, the Bountiful One conquered utterly over all adversaries.

sanskrit: aher yātāraṃ kam apaśya indra hṛdi yat te jaghnuṣo bhīr agacchat | nava ca yan navatiṃ ca sravantīḥ śyeno na bhīto ataro rajāṃsi ||
english: Whom didst thou behold as the avenger of the serpent, O Indra, when fear entered thy heart upon slaying it? Like an undaunted eagle thou didst cross the realms of space where nine and ninety rivers flow.

sanskrit: indro yāto 'vasitasya rājā śamasya ca śṛṅgiṇo vajrabāhuḥ | sed u rājā kṣayati carṣaṇīṇām arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva ||
english: Indra, vajra-armed, has departed — king of the halted, of the still, and of the horned one. He it is who reigns as king over all peoples; like a wheel-rim he has encompassed them all.

sanskrit: yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān devo devān kratunā paryabhūṣat | yasya śuṣmād rodasī abhyasetāṃ nṛmṇasya mahnā sa janāsa indraḥ ||
english: He who, born first of all, was full of mind — the god who surpassed the gods in power of will; at whose vehemence the two world-halves trembled, by the greatness of whose manly might — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ pṛthivīṃ vyadhamānām adṛṃhad yaḥ parvatān prakupitām̐ aramṇāt | yo antarikṣaṃ vimame varīyo yo dyām astabhnāt sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who steadied the earth as it was shaking, who calmed the mountains that were stirred to fury; who measured out the atmosphere more broadly, who propped up the sky — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yo hatvāhim ariṇāt sapta sindhūn yo gā udājad apadhā valasya | yo aśmanor antar agniṃ jajāna saṃvṛk samatsu sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who, having slain the serpent, set the seven rivers free; who drove forth the cattle, having broken open the lair of Vala; who kindled fire within the two stones, undefeated in battles — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yenemā viśvā cyavanā kṛtāni yo dāsaṃ varṇam adharaṃ guhākaḥ | śvaghnīva yo jigīvām̐l lakṣam ādad aryaḥ puṣṭāni sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: By whom all these movable things have been set in motion; who cast the Dāsa colour downward into concealment; who, like a dicing-master winning, seized the prize — the Ārya's prosperities — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaṃ smā pṛcchanti kuha seti ghoram utem āhur naiṣo astīty enam | so aryaḥ puṣṭīr vija ivā mināti śrad asmai dhatta sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: Of whom they ask in dread, "Where is he?" — and of whom they even say, "He does not exist" — he diminishes the Ārya's prosperities like a gambler's stake. Place faith in him — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yo radhrasya coditā yaḥ kṛśasya yo brahmaṇo nādhamānasya kīreḥ | yuktagrāvṇo yo 'vitā suśipraḥ sutasomasya sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who is the impeller of the weak, of the lean; who aids the imploring brahman-poet; the fair-lipped one who is the protector of him whose pressing-stones are yoked and whose Soma is pressed — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yasyāśvāsaḥ pradiśi yasya gāvo yasya grāmā yasya viśve rathāsaḥ | yaḥ sūryaṃ ya uṣasaṃ jajāna yo apāṃ netā sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: Whose are the horses in every direction, whose the cattle, whose the settlements, whose all the chariots; who begot the sun, who begot the dawn, who is the leader of the waters — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaṃ krandasī saṃyatī vihvayete pare 'vara ubhayā amitrāḥ | samānaṃ cid ratham ātasthivāṃsā nānā havete sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: Whom the two battle-cries, meeting in conflict, call upon — both the farther and the nearer, both enemy hosts — even while they have mounted the same chariot, they invoke him separately — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yasmān na rte vijayante janāso yaṃ yudhyamānā avase havante | yo viśvasya pratimānaṃ babhūva yo acyutacyut sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: Without whom people do not conquer; whom those fighting invoke for aid; who has become the counterpart of all the world; who shakes the unshakeable — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ śaśvato mahy eno dadhānān abudhyamānān sarvā jaghāna | yaḥ śardhate nānudadāti śṛdhyāṃ yo dasyor hantā sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who slew all those perpetually bearing great sin, all those who remained unawakened; who does not yield to the insolent their arrogance; who is the slayer of the Dasyu — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ śambaraṃ parvateṣu kṣiyantaṃ catvāriṃśyāṃ śarady anvavindat | ojāyamānaṃ yo ahiṃ jaghāna dānuṃ śayānaṃ sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who found Śambara dwelling in the mountains in the fortieth autumn; who slew the serpent gathering its strength, lying prostrate in the flood — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ śambaraṃ paryacarac chaśībir yo vā vṛkasya nāpibat sutam | antar girau yajamānaṃ bahuṃ janaṃ yas taṃ nāsūrukṣu sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who ranged around Śambara with his missiles, who did not drink the pressed draught of Vṛka; who within the mountain did not rejoice over that abundant folk performing sacrifice — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ saptaraśmir vṛṣabhas tuviṣmān avāsṛjat sartave sapta sindhūn | yo rauhiṇam asphurad vajrabāhur dyām ārohantaṃ sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: He who, the seven-rayed bull, the mighty one, loosed the seven rivers to flow; who, vajra-armed, kicked aside Rauhiṇa as it climbed toward the sky — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: dyāvā cid asmai pṛthivī namete śuṣmāc cid asya parvatā bhayante | yaḥ somapā nicito vajrabāhur yo vajrahastaḥ sa (janāsa indraḥ) ||
english: Even heaven and earth bow down to him; even the mountains tremble from his vehemence; who is a Soma-drinker, collected within, vajra-armed, who holds the vajra in his hand — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ sunvantam avati yaḥ pacantaṃ yaḥ śaṃsantaṃ yaḥ śaśamānam ūtī | yasya brahma vardhanaṃ yasya somo yasyedaṃ rādhaḥ sa janāsa indraḥ ||
english: He who with his aid protects the one pressing Soma, who protects the one cooking the offering, who protects the one reciting the hymn, who protects the one who has toiled; whose sacred formula is the strengthener, whose is the Soma, whose is this bounty — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ sunvate pacate dudhra ā cid vājaṃ dadarṣi sa kilāsi satyaḥ | vayaṃ ta indra viśvaha priyāsaḥ suvīrāso vidatham ā vadema ||
english: Even for him who presses and cooks though refractory, thou dost grant the prize — thou indeed art true. We, thy beloved at all times, O Indra, possessed of good heroes, shall speak forth at the assembly.

sanskrit: jāto vyakhyat pitror upasthe bhuvo na veda janituḥ parasya | taviṣyamāṇo nv ojo akhyad vratā devānāṃ sa janāsa indraḥ ||
english: Born, he gazed about in the lap of his parents; he knew not the womb of a further begetter. Gathering strength, he perceived his might and the ordinances of the gods — he, O people, is Indra.

sanskrit: yaḥ somakāmo haryaśva āsu yasmād rejante bhuvanāni viśvā | yo jaghāna śambaraṃ yaś ca śuṣṇaṃ ya ekavīraḥ sa janāsa indraḥ ||
english: He who, bay-horsed, desires the Soma in these very things; from whom all the worlds tremble; who slew Śambara and who slew Śuṣṇa; who is the sole hero — he, O people, is Indra.
